newsitem.title: PERU: Peru to swear in new presidency minister Monday.
newsitem.headline: Peru to swear in new presidency minister Monday.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori will swear in on Monday his close ally and personal adviser Absalon Vasquez to the key post of presidency minister, Government Palace sources said on Saturday.
The decision to name Vasquez followed the surprise resignation on Friday of Jaime Yoshiyama at the presidency ministry, which oversees social projects, after just 10 months in office.
Yoshiyama, another confidant of Fujimori and regarded as one of the most powerful politicians in the country, cited personal reasons for his resignation.
"I have only words of thanks for a man who has changed the direction of the country, leading it with honour, decisiveness and courage," said Yoshiyama on Saturday in a tribute to Fujimori.
The former Congress president and leading member of Fujimori's New Majority-Change 90 party is expected to return to private business interests.
Vasquez, a former agriculture minister under Fujimori, will control 40 percent of the state budget when he takes over the presidency ministry.
Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi, himself the focus of resignation rumours, insisted on Saturday there was no cabinet crisis despite the shock Yoshiyama's departure caused in local political circles.
"There is not a crisis. The resignation was not due to disagreements with the government," Pandolfi told reporters.
